text:
Evan: Quick brain dump — we need a better per-org throttle model. RPM/TPM alone feels insufficient. Thinking of two axes: sustained rate (tokens/min) + concurrency cap, with a short burst bucket.
Maria: +1. Why tokens/min vs requests/min? most customers vary token lengths a lot.
Evan: Right — requests/min (RPM) protects control-plane ops, tokens/min (TPM) protects GPU spend. We should enforce both.
Jordan: Also add a concurrency cap to prevent hot-orgs from filling worker slots and stomping cold tenants. Concurrency ties directly to latency SLOs.
Tanya: From the console UX POV, we need to show three knobs: Sustained TPM, Burst size, Max concurrency. Defaults per tier (free/paid/enterprise).
Evan: Proposal sketch:
```
policy: {
  sustained_tpm: 12000,    // tokens per minute guaranteed
  burst_tokens: 3000,      // token bucket for short spikes
  burst_window_sec: 60,    // window for burst accounting
  max_concurrency: 25,     // concurrent requests allowed
  cooldown_sec: 300        // penalty cooldown after abusive burst
}
```
Maria: How do we handle sustained overshoot? If org constantly uses bursts, do we throttle to sustained_tpm or apply exponential backoff?
Jordan: I'd prefer a hybrid: soft-throttle (429-lite with Retry-After) for transient overshoot, and after N violations within cooldown window flip to strict enforcement until cooldown expires. Keeps UX friendly.
Tanya: Need telemetry hooks: per-org time-in-soft-throttle, count of hard-enforcements, and estimated extra tokens served (cost). These feed console alerts and billing nudge.
Evan: Edge cases: background jobs that open many short-lived streams will hit concurrency while not using many tokens. Suggest exemption list for jobs with signed intents or separate API keys (but that creates complexity).
Maria: Could we auto-detect streaming patterns and route them through a separate stream pool with higher concurrency per-org but lower per-token throughput?
Jordan: Yes — smart routing can gate them to a stream-optimized pool. But we must keep a global cap per org across pools.
Tanya: UX note: when users see throttled in console, show which axis hit (tokens vs concurrency) + an example request to repro. Helps support.
Evan: Implementation plan:
- Gate at edge gateway v2 (fast path) for token & concurrency checks.
- Emit enforcement events to telemetry (event type: throttle_soft, throttle_hard).
- Control plane stores per-org buckets with TTL, update by gateway.
- Rollout as canary to 5% orgs, track false positives.
Jordan: Quick runtime config snippet idea for gateway:
```json
{"org":"acme","sustained_tpm":12000,"burst_tokens":3000,"max_concurrency":25}
```
Maria: Tests: simulate 10k token/min sustained, 6k burst spike for 2 mins, and 50 concurrent short streams. Validate soft->hard transition.
Tanya: Also need admin override in console to temporarily raise caps during incidents. Audit log every override.
ratebot: Note: enforcement currently lives in gateway-v1. Migration ticket: INF-827 migrate_enforcement_to_gateway_v2. See https://redwood.internal/INF-827
Evan: OK, I'll write a short RFC capturing metrics to track and rollout plan. Tagging you all for review. :thumbsup:
